summary: The first images of Mercury taken from orbit have been received from NASA's MErcury Surface, Space ENvironment, GEochemistry and Ranging (MESSENGER) probe after the spacecraft entered orbit around the planet on March 17, with the first images sent after system examinations at 0520 EDT (0920 UTC). Launched in 2004, MESSENGER passed by Mercury twice in 2008 and once in 2009 and is the first artificial satellite placed in orbit around Mercury; because Mercury is the innermost planet the sun's gravitational attraction altered the spacecraft's approach, requiring a series of maneuvers over three years to put the probe in orbit, and Mariner 10 was the first spacecraft to fly by Mercury in the 1970s. NASA is continuing to release images as they arrive at Earth, and MESSENGER is scheduled to begin its primary mission on April 4 to determine Mercury's geologic composition, study the planet's magnetic field and internal composition, and transmit more than 75,000 images back to Earth.
